Hex World: open questions

2026-10-26. Answer by code, for example "A22 Q1 yes, Q2 half and half". The 17 pieces still awaiting look approval are listed on docs/review/approvals.html (local review server, port 8095).

A19Which Blender pieces next

Q1
Pick the next pieces to build. Each needs an approved reference set first; nothing is queued until you name pieces. My recommendation: B1 and B3 first, then B2.
B1
Boulder and outcrop set: three or four sizes of granite boulders and a low outcrop, as scatter for meadow, forest and coast edges. Fits the new scatter-not-baked rule and fills empty ground cheaply.
B2
Dry-stone walls and hedgerows: field boundaries along meadow and farm edges, placed by rules like fences. Gives farmland structure.
B3
Water-surface props: lily pad clusters and reed beds for ponds, the spring and slow river bends. Pairs with the riverbank scatter just landed.
B4
Forest floor: stumps, mushroom clusters and mossy stones as forest scatter, varying the forest tiles under the trees.

A22Riverbank scatter (landed, batch 28)

Q1
Approve the five new bank props (river_stones, _b, _c, river_reeds, _b) and the rebuilt road bridge, rail bridge and spring. Each river tile now draws a seeded 0 to 4 of them.
Q2
Reeds come up less often than stones: 2 reed props against 9 stone clusters on the five-tile test stretch. Should the reed share go up (for example to half and half)?

A23Bush shine (landed, batch 29)

Q1
Approve the matte verge bushes. The leaf roughness went from about 0.57 to 0.81; nothing else changed (albedo, normals and meshes are byte-identical).
Q2
shrub_forest and shrub_forest_c have the same glossy leaves (roughness 0.50 to 0.64) and show the same sheen. Make them matte too? Holly (shrub_forest_b) stays glossy on purpose. About 30 minutes.
